Subject: Sudden spike in 500s and long tail latency on /v1/generate - urgent

Hi Redwood team,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 500 responses and 5-10s tail latency on our inference calls to /v1/generate around 07:40 PDT today. Error rate jumped from ~0.3% to ~6% and throughput dropped by ~40% during peak. This is impacting our triage workflows.

Attached are some traces and a short HAR export. Can you confirm whether this is related to the model update we rolled last night or infra? We have a late afternoon executive review and need an ETA for mitigation.

Thanks,
Ellie

On Sat, Apr 18, 2027 at 08:27, tessa.morgan@redwood.com wrote:
> Folks — forwarding Ellie. High priority. Quick read: sudden error-rate and tail latency spike for Nebula endpoints starting ~07:40 PDT.

Investigating now. Early findings:
- The customer is routed to a dedicated DHA pool (dha-us-west-2-07) — that pool saw a CPU scheduling pressure spike and kernel I/O stalls between 07:38–07:55.
- We concurrently rolled a micro-quantization kernel change to all pools at 03:20 UTC last night; can cause higher decode CPU if fallback path triggers.
- Logs show increased KV cache misses for sequences longer than 1k tokens, which matches Nebula’s largest job.

Action plan (first 30m):
1) Revert the micro-quantization change on dha-us-west-2-07 and fallback to previous kernel.
2) Temporarily increase concurrency limits for Nebula’s model route to reduce queueing (shifts some load).
3) Collect a full support bundle (metrics, kernel traces, agent logs) and share with Nebula.

Connor — please run the revert and capture the timeframe. I’ll coordinate with Marissa for the customer message.

Vivek
SVP, Serving Engineering

From: connor.obrien@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden spike in 500s and long tail latency on /v1/generate - urgent

Started the rollback on dha-us-west-2-07 at 09:29 PDT. Progress:
- Kernel revert applied to worker set A (30% of nodes) at 09:31 — initial telemetry shows error rate falling to ~1.2% and p95 latency improving.
- Rolling to remaining nodes in 10-minute windows to avoid cold-start amplification.
- Snapshot of queued requests saved and uploaded to the incident folder.

Uploading support bundle now (will post link).

Connor O’Brien
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Ellie / Mateo — quick update from Redwood:
- We detected a CPU scheduling/I/O pressure event on the dedicated pool serving your traffic at ~07:38 PDT; an overnight micro-quantization kernel change increased decoding CPU in fallback paths.
- We rolled back the kernel change starting 09:29 PDT; initial telemetry shows error rate reduced to ~1% and p95 latency trending down.
- We’ve increased concurrency limits for your model route and will monitor for 2h.

Next steps for Nebula:
1) Please validate your end-to-end flows — we saved queued request snapshots and traces in the support bundle.
2) We propose a short (30-min) touchpoint at 14:00 PDT to confirm stability and walk the mitigation steps. If you prefer earlier, we can jump on a 1:1.

Links: support bundle (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1NebulaIncidentLogs) — includes latency_metrics_q2.csv and traces.

I'll be on the 14:00 touchpoint and will share a mutual action plan after we confirm stability.

Marissa Cole

Subject: Quick post-touchpoint summary & exec note

Hi Ellie, Mateo — thanks for taking the 14:00 PDT check-in. Short summary for your execs and ours:

What happened:
- An overnight micro-quantization kernel rollout increased decode CPU in fallback paths for long sequences on your dedicated pool, causing KV cache misses and I/O scheduling pressure. This manifested as elevated 500s and a long-tail p99 latency increase.

What we did:
- Rolled back the micro-change on the affected pool (09:29–09:55 PDT), increased route concurrency, and stabilized node scheduling. Connor and Vivek led the fix.

Current state:
- Error rate is down to ~0.8% system-wide for your routes; p95 latency is back within SLA targets, p99 shows improvement but we’ll continue monitoring for 24 hours.

Follow-ups / commitments:
- Redwood will run a targeted regression test against your largest jobset and provide a post-mortem within 48 hours.
- We’ll schedule a model-variant compatibility check before any future kernel or quantization rollouts affecting dedicated pools.
- Mutual action plan attached (mutual_action_plan_nebula_v2.pdf).

If you want an exec-to-exec note packaged for your leadership, we can draft one and include timeline bullets.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll keep this as a top priority until you’re fully green.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
